independence: These observations were formed from this object's original, fixed target, GLOBAL style reference, actual original collection and independently registered source replay. No editor proposal or other-object aesthetic review was read.

original.identity: A compact cobalt blue rock bank: one broad high crown, offset side shoulder and lower overlapping boulders. It is quiet environmental scenery rather than an actor or modular cliff join.
original.shapeVolume: The main crown reads clearly, but near-vertical lower facets and flat planar bases produce a blocky pillar impression. Repeated octagonal bevel language makes secondary rocks feel mechanically similar. N and W merge the lower masses into large rectangular dark fronts; E and S show the small pieces more clearly.
original.color: Cobalt and lighter blue upper faces over deep navy lower faces preserve the underwater palette. The top is already strongly saturated and luminous relative to the dark base.
original.lightingHighlights: Broad crowns are readable, but the lower halves become dark unmodulated bands, particularly N and W. Hard plane boundaries dominate rather than soft rolling edge highlights.
original.materialDetail: Almost all information comes from large faces and height shading. No authored surface detail or gentle edge rounding is visible. Small isolated details should not replace the mass hierarchy.
original.useSize: At half logical scale (64 px per cell), the boulder hierarchy still reads, but N and W become dark bottom rectangles beneath bright caps. This is an observed baseline, not a requirement to retain that darkness.

valuableOutcomes: More organic interlocking broad blue stones with varied crown and shoulder shapes and softened, purposeful contours.
Softer face-to-face transitions and broad upper highlights that describe volume.
Enough subtle blue material separation to read stone masses without flat dead patches.
Sparse rounded chips or depressions may add crafted character if they survive use size and stay quiet.
limits: Its white-cyan edge network is much brighter and glossier than the original; literal glowing seams would compete with actors and contradict quiet background depth.
Its canvas is 926x1699 rather than the native 384x704 published frame. Its placement, proportions, contact and camera cannot define registration or a new size budget.
A single S-like view does not establish the unseen N/E/W surfaces, native connectivity or support.

globalStyle: The plant reference uses generous native volume, clear large forms, soft rounded edges and restrained broad highlights with rich palette separation. Its green/gold palette is style-only; this rock remains cobalt blue.

nativeFindings.enabledMeasurement: Collection ancestry and all owned objects enabled in actual scene/view layer before depsgraph sampling. Raw authored and evaluated bounds measured separately and are equal.
nativeFindings.nominalHeightConflict: Catalog height is 1.05, while the actual crown has purposeful uneven top vertices reaching 1.075. Root reconciliation is required before choosing the design envelope; do not silently trim to 1.05 or treat hidden stale bounds as a lock.
nativeFindings.camera: Saved startup is chef-noor at frame4 with a 35-degree camera and 768x1280 frame. Own registered record is 55.00798 degrees, non-square pixel aspect 1.22065556, native768x1408, published384x704, logical192x352, root96/256. Independently measured replay recovers that calibration.
nativeFindings.sourceState: 4 closed meshes, each32 vertices/26 faces, all flat normals, no modifiers, UVs, shape keys, armatures or constraints. Materials are owned by these4 meshes, no owned image textures or libraries.
nativeFindings.temporal: Actual owned object/data/material/node-tree channels have no actions, NLA or drivers. Static frame1 is the only required phase; no invented motion or closure frame is needed.
nativeFindings.support: All4 rocks have finite polygonal base faces at Z0. Their union is a grounded irregular bank, not a full opaque1x1 tile. No actual sockets or modular ports exist.
